# How to Create AI Cooking Videos That Get Views on Social Media

Cooking channels live or die by posting cadence, and editing every recipe by hand kills momentum. The practical question is which AI tools auto-cut, caption, and resize your cooking footage into scroll-stopping clips.

## The decision before you

Before comparing features, decide what "good" means for you. 9 of these are Free or Freemium, so cost is rarely the blocker; the real filters are your skill level and the content you ship. 0 are Paid, usually signaling deeper features. Read each section for strengths and honest limits, then match a tool to one repeating task.

## The tools worth considering

### VEED.io

[[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]] is a Freemium video tool for Beginners, Social Media, Marketing. It handles social Media Reels and Course Video Editing, and its key strength is that no software to install — everything runs in the browser with automatic cloud saving. The honest limit: browser-based means performance depends on internet speed and browser capabilities. At a beginner level, new users can get value on day one without a steep learning curve.

### AI Video Editor

[[link:/tools/612|AI Video Editor]] is a Freemium video tool for Video Editing, Content Creation, YouTube. It handles automated Cuts and Scene Detection, and its key strength is that automation handles repetitive editing work for solo creators. The honest limit: automated cuts may not match a specific creative vision. At a intermediate level, expect a short setup period before it fits smoothly into your workflow.

### Fliki

[[link:/tools/278|Fliki]] is a Freemium video tool for Text-to-Video, AI Voices, Marketing. It handles blog-to-Video and Social Snippets, and its key strength is that text-to-video workflow needs no filming or editing experience. The honest limit: stock-visual matching can feel generic on niche topics. At a beginner level, new users can get value on day one without a steep learning curve.

### InShot AI

[[link:/tools/1478|InShot AI]] is a Freemium video tool for Mobile, Reels, TikTok. It handles reel Editing and Auto Captions, and its key strength is that mobile-first workflow lets creators shoot and edit anywhere. The honest limit: phone-based editing struggles with longer or complex projects. At a beginner level, new users can get value on day one without a steep learning curve.

### ElevenLabs

[[link:/tools/8|ElevenLabs]] is a Freemium audio tool for Professionals, High Quality, Content Creation. It handles audiobook Narration and Game Character Voices, and its key strength is that voice quality and emotional range are among the best available today. The honest limit: free tier is limited; serious production requires a paid plan. At a intermediate level, expect a short setup period before it fits smoothly into your workflow.

### Murf AI

[[link:/tools/78|Murf AI]] is a Freemium audio tool for Content Creation, Beginners, Quick Results. It handles corporate Training Videos and Podcast Intros & Outros, and its key strength is that 120+ voices with granular control over pitch, speed, pause, and emphasis — studio-grade output. The honest limit: free plan limited to 10 minutes of voice generation — not enough for serious projects. At a beginner level, new users can get value on day one without a steep learning curve.

### CapCut Pro AI

[[link:/tools/957|CapCut Pro AI]] is a Freemium video tool for Video Editing, Short Video, Social Media. It handles auto Subtitles and One-Click Templates, and its key strength is that automatic subtitles remove tedious manual captioning work from editing. The honest limit: templates can make videos look similar across creators. At a beginner level, new users can get value on day one without a steep learning curve.

### Opus Clip

[[link:/tools/1534|Opus Clip]] is a Freemium video tool for Content Creators, Podcasters, YouTubers. It handles podcast Clips and YouTube Repurposing, and its key strength is that automates clip selection from hours of long-form footage. The honest limit: automatic selections can miss important context-heavy discussion moments. At a beginner level, new users can get value on day one without a steep learning curve.

### CapCut

[[link:/tools/1512|CapCut]] is a Freemium video tool for Short-Form Video, Auto Captions, Social Media. It handles auto Captions and Background Removal, and its key strength is that core editing features are free on desktop and mobile. The honest limit: some advanced effects and features sit behind the paid tier. At a beginner level, new users can get value on day one without a steep learning curve.

## How to choose

Start where the friction is highest. If you are unsure, begin with [[link:/tools/612|AI Video Editor]] and [[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]], since both cover common, repeatable work and are approachable for most skill levels. From there, add one specialist only when a task repeats enough to justify it. Do not adopt a Paid tool until a Free or Freemium option has clearly hit its limit for you.

## A workflow you can chain today

Record the cook once, auto-edit in [[link:/tools/612|AI Video Editor]], add captions and trims in [[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]], voice steps with [[link:/tools/78|Murf AI]], then export vertical versions via [[link:/tools/1478|InShot AI]].

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Treating AI output as final. Drafts, voices, and clips still need a human pass for accuracy, tone, and legal or brand fit.
- Ignoring skill level. Some tools here assume a beginner workflow, while a few expect an advanced setup; the mismatch wastes time.
- Stacking too many subscriptions. With several Paid options in this list, trial the Free or Freemium tiers before committing to a monthly plan.
- Skipping verification. AI can invent details or produce inconsistent results, so always review before publishing to a real audience.

## FAQ

### What is the fastest way to edit cooking footage?

[[link:/tools/612|AI Video Editor]] detects scenes and [[link:/tools/957|CapCut Pro AI]] adds auto subtitles, cutting manual work.

### Do I need a separate voice tool?

[[link:/tools/78|Murf AI]] or [[link:/tools/8|ElevenLabs]] can narrate steps if your video is silent.

### Which format performs best?

Vertical clips via [[link:/tools/1478|InShot AI]] and [[link:/tools/1512|CapCut]] suit Reels and Shorts.

### How do I keep recipes accurate?

Always write the ingredient list yourself; use AI only for editing and pacing.

## Final takeaway

The best result comes from pairing one AI tool per stage of your work and reviewing the output yourself. Use the links above to try the options that match your task, and expand your stack only as real repeats appear.
tldr: Record once, auto-edit with one tool, then export vertical versions for each platform.
